description.value: Hebbia is a private American technology company in New York City that builds AI and automation tools for financial and legal research. George Sivulka founded it in August 2020.
Hebbia is an AI company that builds tools for finance and other professional services.
Hebbia is a New York-based AI company founded in 2020, and its main customers are financial firms.

product_description.value: Max, an AI analyst for investment research that lets teams share AI work across a firm, and Matrix, a tool for running research at scale with source documents attached.

Max is an AI analyst for deal teams and Matrix manages AI-driven research at scale; integrations include SEC filings, earnings transcripts, FactSet, S&P Capital IQ, PitchBook, SharePoint, Box, Salesforce and Snowflake.

Its main product, Matrix, analyzes PDFs, spreadsheets and slide decks and answers plain-language questions with linked source citations; in 2025 Hebbia acquired FlashDocs, which generates slide decks.
Flagship product is Matrix; profiles also describe AI agents that break complex tasks into smaller actions and a neural search feature.

business_model_description.value: No pricing or subscription terms stated; the only call to action is Request a demo, which suggests an enterprise sales model.
Implies enterprise software sold to financial and legal firms; no pricing or revenue model stated.

customer_description.value: Investors, bankers, lawyers, consultants and Fortune 500 companies; named clients include Morgan Stanley, MetLife, Centerview, OHA, 26North, Rice Management Company, New Mountain Capital and Latham & Watkins.

Investing, investment banking, legal and professional services, and corporate finance strategy; named clients include Morgan Stanley, MetLife, Centerview, OHA, New Mountain Capital and Latham & Watkins.
Asset managers, investment banks and private equity firms use Matrix for due diligence, M&A and investment research; law firms use it for contract clause review and M&A diligence.
Powers investment decisions for BlackRock, KKR, Carlyle, Centerview and 40% of the world's largest asset managers.
Third-party profiles say its users include professionals in finance, law, government and pharma.

revenue.value: About $13M in 2024 revenue (Latka estimate); Built In attributes roughly $13M to TechCrunch as of mid-2024.
